title: The Unexpected Semester
premise: Coral Villalobos has spent her whole life as the only out kid in Marisol Flats, a town of nine hundred that owes its existence to her great-grandmother's founding recipes. When she discovers her grandmother's recipe box contains coded directions to the town's secret founding covenant, she learns the 'tradition' that saved the town during the Dust Bowl was built on a betrayal: the covenant's protections were stolen from a neighboring family whose land was taken to make the deal possible. As the covenant's centennial renewal approaches and time runs out to either renew it honestly or let the town's water rights collapse, Coral must choose between loyalty to the community that has never fully accepted her and the truth that could save it differently. She ends the covenant as it was and rebuilds it on returned land and public amends, discovering that justice outside the law is slower, messier, and finally hers to shape.
about_author: Gideon Delacroix is the pen name of a former small-town newspaper reporter who spent three years covering water disputes in the American Southwest before turning to fiction. They write young adult stories about kids who inherit more than they bargained for.

chapters.title: Ninety-Eight Days
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. She counts down to graduation while working the diner counter, enduring small-town slights with practiced numbness. Establishes her best friend Theo, her exhausted mother, and her longing to leave. Emotional beat: suffocated but surviving, she believes the town has nothing left to give her.

chapters.title: The Recipe Box
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. Sorting her late grandmother's kitchen, she finds a recipe card for 'Founding Pie' whose instructions are nonsense as cooking and unmistakable as a cipher. A second card references a date three weeks away: the centennial. Emotional beat: curiosity cracking open grief.

chapters.title: Founders' Day, Every Year
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. At the centennial planning meeting, she watches the town council guard the 'Old Covenant' ceremony with unusual intensity, and councilman Ray Sandoval warns her off her grandmother's papers. Emotional beat: the town she wanted to escape suddenly wants something from her.

chapters.title: Card by Card
chapters.summary: Coral's POV, with Theo. She and Theo decode the cards using the town archive's founding documents, discovering the covenant is a literal contract binding water rights to an annual ritual. Emotional beat: the thrill of a secret that finally belongs to her.

chapters.title: The Missing Name
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. The covenant names four founding families, but the land deed history shows a fifth parcel absorbed with no record of sale. The name on the original homestead: Okafor. Emotional beat: the first cold drop of doubt.

chapters.title: Miss Okafor's Porch
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. She interviews Adaeze Okafor, ninety-one, the town's other outsider, who goes quiet when shown the cards and says only: 'Ask what your grandmother was paying for.' Emotional beat: an alliance neither expected, offered carefully.

chapters.title: What Grandma Was Paying For
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. A hidden letter from her grandmother reveals the truth: the 1925 covenant traded Okafor water rights for town survival, and every generation of Villalobos women has kept the secret as 'stewards.' Emotional beat: inheritance curdles into burden.

chapters.title: Renewal or Ruin
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. She learns the covenant expires at the centennial ceremony; if not renewed, the town loses its water rights entirely. Sandoval pressures her to renew it as her grandmother's heir. Emotional beat: the countdown becomes real, and it's her signature they need.

chapters.title: Theo's Question
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Theo, whose family works Sandoval's fields, wrestles with what Coral's discovery means for people who'd lose everything if the town fails. He asks Coral whether the truth is worth the cost. Emotional beat: loyalty and truth pull in opposite directions.

chapters.title: The Archive at Night
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. Breaking into the archive, she finds Sandoval's family was complicit in the 1925 deal and he's been quietly buying Okafor-adjacent land, planning to profit from the collapse. Emotional beat: righteous anger, and a plan forming.

chapters.title: Photographs
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. She documents everything, but Adaeze warns her: the town will call her a traitor before they'll call her right, as they once called Adaeze's father a liar. Emotional beat: Coral confronts the price of being the one who tells.

chapters.title: The Leak
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. A photocopy surfaces at the diner; the town splits into camps overnight. Her mother, terrified, begs her to sign the renewal and keep the peace. Emotional beat: the first real rupture at home.

chapters.title: Sandoval's Offer
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. Sandoval privately offers to restore the Okafor name to the record if Coral signs the renewal first, a deal that saves the town but buries the truth permanently. Emotional beat: a genuinely tempting lie, and Coral almost takes it.

chapters.title: Adaeze's Testimony
chapters.summary: Adaeze's POV. In her own voice, Adaeze recounts the 1925 betrayal her father lived and died carrying. She tells Coral she doesn't want revenge, she wants the land, or the truth, before she dies. Emotional beat: grief transformed into demand.

chapters.title: The Town Meeting
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. At a packed emergency meeting, Coral presents the covenant's history. Half the town turns on her; the sheriff, her uncle, asks her to stop for the family's sake. Emotional beat: standing alone in the room she grew up in.

chapters.title: What the Water Remembers
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. Researching the aquifer itself, she finds a third path: the original Okafor parcel sits on the strongest well water. Returning it isn't charity, it's the only renewal that works. Emotional beat: hope with a blueprint.

chapters.title: The Sabotage
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. The recipe box and her evidence vanish from the diner; Sandoval denies it, but the timing is his. With the ceremony in four days, Coral has only memory and allies. Emotional beat: despair, then Theo showing up with a plan.

chapters.title: Reconstruction
chapters.summary: Coral, Theo, and Adaeze's POV braided. The three rebuild the case from Adaeze's family Bible, church records, and Coral's memory, drafting a new covenant: returned land, public amends, shared water. Emotional beat: justice built by hand, outside any courtroom.

chapters.title: Centennial Eve
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. Sandoval, cornered by the evidence resurfacing in the newspaper and the county clerk's office, makes his move: he'll renew the old covenant himself using a forged heir signature. Emotional beat: the clock runs out at midnight.

chapters.title: The Ceremony
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. On stage before all nine hundred, Coral interrupts the renewal, presents the truth, and offers the new covenant, with Adaeze beside her and the county clerk confirming the land transfer. Sandoval's forgery is exposed. Emotional beat: the climax, spoken aloud to everyone at once.

chapters.title: After the Vote
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs. The town votes, narrowly, to ratify the new covenant. Some neighbors don't forgive; some do. Her mother finally reads her grandmother's letter and weeps. Emotional beat: the cost acknowledged, the repair begun.

chapters.title: Day One of Something
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. Graduation day. Coral still plans to leave, but now for a semester, not a sentence, and she's leaving a town that knows its own history. Adaeze hands her the recipe box, restewardship passing on. Emotional beat: belonging chosen, not inherited, and a future she authored.
